about: Competitive analysis for Web Summit 2026 (Silvio's ask, 5 November 2026), by outreach@web-summit.silvio with two research agents. Each company's headline and offer are from its own website, read on 5 November 2026 through a tool that summarises pages, so quotes may be trimmed. 'Where we differ' and 'what we learn' are RiskMandate's own view, not statements by the companies. 'web_summit' says how we know they attend: 'Web Summit's pages' (the team's company map, data/companies.json, read 1 November), 'their own site', or 'a third-party list' (not confirmed by Web Summit).

us.name: RiskMandate
us.headline: Give agents access. Not free rein.
us.offer: An Agent Behaviour Policy for each agent: what it can reach, what the business authorised, the gap between the two and the controls that hold, signed off as a licence to operate.
us.action: Try it in five minutes, nothing to install; one-off prices from £10 to £1,500 per agent.

stages.label: Before the agent acts
stages.text: What the agent can reach, what it was asked to do, the gap, and who signs it off.

stages.label: While it acts
stages.text: Tokens, access, spending caps and filters that enforce the rules: each one a barrier an Agent Behaviour Policy can name.

stages.label: After it acts
stages.text: Signed receipts, proof of deletion and quality scores: evidence that the mandate held.

companies.name: Summit Cognitive
companies.headline: When your AI makes a decision, can you prove what happened?
companies.offer: Decision Receipts: a signed record of each AI-assisted decision (what it saw, what it decided, which rule applied, who approved it), checkable offline.
companies.action: See a sample receipt; a design-partner pilot with a published price.
companies.differ: Their receipt records a decision after it is made. Our policy says what the agent may do before it acts, and who signed that off.
companies.learn: A sample anyone can open and check in one click.

companies.name: Airia
companies.headline: Discover, secure, govern, and optimize every AI agent.
companies.offer: An enterprise platform that finds the AI in use, enforces controls on agents, produces governance documents and also builds agents.
companies.web_summit: Web Summit's pages (a session by its CEO)
companies.differ: A platform you buy into. We are one record per agent, readable by the board and the insurer, that starts in five minutes.
companies.learn: Four verbs that cover the whole job.

companies.name: Hexamind (Hexgate)
companies.headline: Take back control of your AI agents.
companies.offer: Hexgate, an open-source (MIT) layer that checks every tool call an agent makes against a signed policy, with an audit trail.
companies.action: pip install hexgate; book a demo.
companies.differ: Hexgate enforces a policy. We say what the policy should be, and show the gate as evidence that it holds. A natural joint demo.

companies.name: Polygraf AI
companies.headline: AI Behavioral Control Plane
companies.offer: A control layer between people, agents and AI systems that inspects content, enforces policy and stops sensitive data reaching models; on-premises or air-gapped.
companies.action: Not read: its site did not answer our tool.
companies.differ: It controls what goes in and out of AI systems. We record what each agent is authorised to do.

companies.name: Conscium
companies.headline: Test your AI Agent, in any scenario.
companies.offer: Verifyax tests agents in simulation for accuracy, safety, security and compliance, before and after deployment.
companies.web_summit: Web Summit's pages (a session by its co-founder)
companies.differ: They test what an agent does. We write the mandate the test checks against, and license the result.

companies.name: Delinea
companies.headline: See every identity. Understand every risk. Control every action.
companies.offer: Privileged access for people, machines and AI agents, with just-in-time authorisation of each agent action.
companies.differ: Their record is who accessed what. Ours says what the access is for, and where it is more than the task needs.

companies.name: Arsia Labs
companies.headline: AI infrastructure. Built for accountability.
companies.offer: An open protocol for signed messages between agents, with EU rules (GDPR, the AI Act, DORA) written into it, plus a gateway and a proxy. Based in Portugal.
companies.differ: A protocol for engineers. Ours is a record a business signs.
companies.learn: Name the EU regulations in the product itself.

companies.name: Descope
companies.headline: Identity journeys for customers and AI agents.
companies.offer: Login and authorisation for apps, now for agents and MCP servers, with scopes per agent and per tool.
companies.web_summit: Web Summit's pages (a session on securing agents)
companies.differ: They issue the scopes. We decide which scopes each agent should have, and why.
companies.learn: Research numbers that make the risk concrete.

companies.name: Keyban (Agent Wallet)
companies.headline: Your AI agents pay. You stay in control.
companies.offer: A payment account per agent, with caps, allowed payees and human approval, enforced in the infrastructure rather than the prompt.
companies.differ: Money is one line of an agent's reach. We cover all of it.
companies.learn: Concrete demo scenes a visitor follows in seconds.

companies.name: Forg3t Protocol
companies.headline: Who controls what your AI knows?
companies.offer: Removes selected data from AI models and hands over a signed before-and-after for a regulator.
companies.action: Request a demo; a deletion-risk check.
companies.differ: They cover the data a model holds. We cover what an agent may do.
companies.learn: A short, sharp hook, and labels that say how each fact is known.

companies.name: TrustScale
companies.headline: Configure and measure AI against your own criteria.
companies.offer: Evaluation and assurance of what AI produces, with a branded TrustScore and expert human review.
companies.action: Book a meeting; a free try.
companies.web_summit: Web Summit's pages (its CEO on a panel)
companies.differ: They score what an AI says. We govern what an agent can do.
companies.learn: A named score. Ours is on the roadmap: the Insurability Index.
